It's not about technology for its own sake. It's about being able to implement your ideas.

Turbo Pascal 3 for MS-DOS was released in September 1986. Being version 3, there were lesser releases prior to it and flashier ones after, but 3 was a solid representation of the Turbo Pascal experience: a full Pascal compiler, including extensions that it made it practical for commercial use, tightly integrated with an editor. And the whole thing was lightning fast, orders of magnitude faster at building projects than Microsoft's compilers.

The entire Turbo Pascal 3.02 executable--the compiler and IDE--was 39,731 bytes. How does that stack up in 2011 terms? Here are some things that Turbo Pascal is smaller than, as of October 30, 2011:

The minified version of jquery 1.6 (90,518 bytes).

The yahoo.com home page (219,583 bytes).

The image of the white iPhone 4S at apple.com (190,157 bytes).

zlib.h in the Mac OS X Lion SDK (80,504 bytes).

The touch command under OS X Lion (44,016 bytes).

Various vim quick reference cards as PDFs. ( This one is 47,508 bytes.)

The compiled code for the Erlang R14B02 parser ( erl_parse.beam , 286,324 bytes).

The Wikipedia page for C++ (214,251 bytes).

(If you liked this, you might like A Personal History of Compilation Speed .)

I'm James Hague, a recovering programmer who has been designing video games since the 1980s. Programming Without Being Obsessed With Programming and Organizational Skills Beat Algorithmic Wizardry are good starting points. For the older stuff, try the 2012 Retrospective .

items.title: FreeBSD bhyve Live Migration: Moving VMs Between Hosts
items.content:
This project presents a first working state for live migration of bhyve guests on FreeBSD 15.1. A running amd64 guest can move between two hosts over TCP while continuing to run; it is paused only for the final stop-and-copy phase. The work builds on bhyve's experimental snapshot support and adds dirty-page tracking in the vmm kernel module together with a migration protocol in bhyve and bhyvectl.

Live migration of a VM in FreeBSD with bhyve

I previously discussed the state of bhyve live migration, its historical development, existing limitations, and why it matters for the future of FreeBSD virtualization in my article bhyve on FreeBSD and VM Live Migration – Quo vadis? .

The goal is deliberately practical: make it possible to test, discuss, and improve a real implementation rather than discuss live migration only in the abstract. The current code and test tooling are being published as a WIP RFC so that the next steps can be shaped in the open. A more detailed demonstration of a VM being live migrated can be watched on my YouTube channel .

Live migration is an important building block for enterprise virtualisation. It enables host maintenance, hardware replacement, load balancing, and failure-domain management with far less disruption to workloads. It is also central to the Sylve project, which aims to offer a Proxmox-like virtualisation solution for FreeBSD. Migration is not an optional convenience in that kind of platform; it is one of the capabilities that makes clustered operations practical.

It is equally important for BoxyBSD, where I offer free BSD-based VPS instances to individuals. Without a credible migration path, routine host work can require a guest outage. That makes live migration a current show stopper for the project, and is why this work is being pushed toward a testable, reviewable state.

The source starts with a pre-copy phase. It sends populated guest memory, then repeatedly obtains a bitmap of pages changed since the previous scan and sends only those pages. Once the remaining dirty set fits the configured downtime target, stops shrinking, or reaches the configured round limit, bhyve pauses the guest and its devices. It then sends the final dirty pages and the existing snapshot state for the vCPUs, kernel state, and emulated devices.

The destination validates the basic VM geometry, receives memory and state, restores it, and reports that it is ready. Only then does the source send GO , the commit point. Before GO , a failed migration can resume the source guest. The destination does not start the guest if it does not receive that commit message. A warm, stop-and-copy mode is available too, which is useful both as a fallback and as a comparison baseline.

Pre-copy and warm migration: live pre-copy is configurable with downtime and maximum-round controls; explicit stop-and-copy migration is also supported.

Multi-vCPU protocol support: the migration handshake carries the guest vCPU count, the destination refuses a count mismatch, and all guest vCPUs are paused and resumed as part of migration. The published test bed has primarily exercised a one-vCPU guest, so multi-vCPU stress and race testing remain required before making broader claims.

Memory consistency checks: dirty-page tracking covers guest and mapped emulation writes through page dirty state, while vmm write holds are recorded separately. The test workload rewrites and verifies guest memory and reports any missing or stale page as a mismatch. Repeated ping-pong migrations have been used to check that the workload continues without errors.

Disk-write validation: a guest-side workload repeatedly writes and fsyncs files, verifies checksums, and is checked again after a cold reboot. This is intended to exercise the device pause, drain, and restore path.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Nvidia deliberately kept GPU prices high through circular financing deals, report claims
items.content:
Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years.

TechSpot means tech analysis and advice you can trust .

Connecting the dots: The AI boom has been widely blamed for GPU prices spinning out of control over the past year. Following Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia,new information suggests that this was the goal of the former CEO's business strategy, which has long drawn accusations of circular financing.

A recent Wall Street Journal profile of Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress has shed more light on how Nvidia controversially financed its own customers to drive the AI boom. According to the report, the company pushed for more deals in mid-to-late 2026 to absorb an oversupply of TSMC wafers and keep GPU prices high.

Since at least last year, Nvidia has been accused of prolonging the AI boom by supporting the companies that buy its chips. Co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang, along with CFO Kress, even went so far as to defend the company against comparisons to Enron, which used similar tactics to illegally obscure its debt before its 2001 collapse.

Also read: GPU Prices Are Spiraling Out of Control - Q4 2026 Update

Behind the scenes, Kress expressed concern about the scale of the deals Nvidia had inked with cloud providers and major AI companies like OpenAI. Nvidia pushed ahead anyway, but by summer 2026, the company was wondering whether it had pushed too far amid an "avalanche" of semiconductors it had ordered from TSMC.

It was around this time that Huang berated Kress, calling her "a deer in headlights," according to someone familiar with the matter. Nvidia began to slow down, downsize, and pause some of its financing deals, including one with OpenAI that originally included a $250 billion backstop for the world's largest data center.

Nearly 150,000 people sign petition requesting Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO

Without Jensen Huang, is it game over for GeForce?

AI data centers have siphoned off DRAM and NAND manufacturing capacity traditionally used for RAM and storage in consumer devices, inflating prices. Nvidia's GeForce GPUs have been hit especially hard, with prices often exceeding 160% of their original MSRP. The company's flagship RTX 5090 has become unobtainable because Nvidia has directed its VRAM and semiconductors toward data center GPUs.

As its financial support deals wound down, Huang became worried about the company's stock market valuation, with its average monthly stock multiple falling far behind those of other large tech companies.

Related: Without Jensen Huang, is it game over for GeForce?

Colette Kress, Interim CEO and Executive VP and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Nvidia.

At a Berlin conference, the former CEO told major clients a story about a busy Japanese soup vendor who refused to give him a second serving after he had waited in a long line, saying the vendor had too many customers and not enough soup. Huang used the story to highlight the value of maintaining a diverse customer base and keeping prices high, suggesting that Nvidia's circular financing strategy inflated GPU prices by creating the perception of high demand.

The story emerged after Huang's resignation following the revelation of multiple extramarital affairs. One was with Alice Huang (no relation), whose company, Megaspeed, was suspected by US intelligence of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of export regulations. While some allege that she is a spy for Beijing, President Trump and the Justice Department said that hasn't been determined.

items.title: Same-window official baselines for hidden model degradation on LLM API relays
items.content:
Folkbench has launched model degradation detection inside the Integrity Monitor . Conventional model leaderboards evaluate what a model can achieve under official or single-host conditions, while typical API relay directories stop at listed pricing, HTTP uptime, and response latency. Neither answers the central operational question for relay users: when a model is served through a third-party API relay, do its reasoning depth, constraint adherence, and model-level behavior remain consistent with the direct official API?

To close that evaluation gap, Folkbench embeds an automated probe suite spanning current-events and model-fingerprint dimensions, calibrated continuously against independent direct official API keys within the same measurement windows. Anchoring third-party relay behavior to a live official baseline converts subjective suspicion into observable, reviewable public signals.

Key elements of this capability include:

In a standard relay architecture, an intermediary gateway sits between the caller and the upstream model lab. Most relays simply forward requests and meter usage, yet cost pressure or peak-hour routing can introduce three forms of degradation that network telemetry alone cannot distinguish:

Figure 1: Green surface connectivity (HTTP `200`, low initial latency, fluent short replies) does not guarantee intact capability delivery. Gateway routing swaps, lowered reasoning budgets, and truncated histories occur below standard network telemetry.

All three share an important property: surface connectivity remains intact . The endpoint still returns HTTP 200 , casual prompts produce fluent replies, and shorter reasoning traces can even make responses appear faster. Standard availability and latency checks cannot distinguish a genuine flagship run from a trimmed or substituted one. At the same time, sampling randomness means isolated failures happen even on healthy endpoints—as analyzed in [Did the Model Really Get Dumber?](/en/blog/did-the-model-get-dumber/), individual screenshots cannot separate normal variance from systemic degradation.

When users suspect a route has degraded, two common manual tests fail under real-world relay routing:

Figure 2: Two structural failure modes of manual relay checks. On the left, a gateway system prompt overrides identity statements regardless of backend weights. On the right, gateway filters recognize repeated static prompts and return static caches or route checks to a clean whitelist while keeping daily traffic degraded.

Reliable degradation detection therefore requires prompts that cannot be pre-cached or memorized, paired with signals that go beyond whether a single final answer happens to look right.

To detect hidden drift accurately, Folkbench separates evaluation prompts and protocol telemetry into two complementary dimensions collected together in each test window.

Figure 3: Same-window architecture combining dynamic current-events probes (blocking static caching and stale fallbacks) with model-fingerprint telemetry (tracking probe agreement, input tokens, reasoning tokens, fingerprint fields, and cache checks) across isolated official direct keys and target `model × service group` routes.

Current-events probes incorporate recent real-world timelines, newly surfaced context, and time-sensitive relationships into structured reasoning tasks. Unlike static trivia or unchanging puzzles, these prompts evolve continuously:

Even if a substitute model answers an ordinary objective question correctly—or the true model runs with half its thinking budget removed—final-answer accuracy alone may miss the shift.

Model-fingerprint probes target behavioral patterns that remain distinct across model families under multi-step constraints, strict formatting boundaries, and structured reasoning paths. Alongside output alignment, Folkbench records protocol-level vital signs returned by the endpoint:

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Emacs Is My Browser
items.content:
In my ever-increasing desire to use emacs as my sole computing environment , I have started to take browsing the web inside it far more seriously. Where I previously had thought EWW to be a niceity but far from capable, after using it for a few days it seems to be useable for about 85-90% of use cases - even on the javascript riddled hellhole that is the internet.

I have seen in my own use of the modern browser (chromium/firefox) that it is far too easy to get distracted - too easy to get off track and fall down rabbit holes that take over my day. There are infinite suggestions as to how I should spend my time, uncountable shiny objects that take my eye off the prize that is Creativity and Depth. This has been momentously negated with EWW (or any terminal browser, lynx or browsh for the non-emacs users).

In addition to this, my belief is that we should make strides toward leaving behind Layer 8 of the internet - the limiting frontends of social platforms and locked away corners of the net that limit actual discourse (Discord, I’m looking at you). We have given up far too much to big tech platforms, and gotten nothing of value in return, to the point that many now think the internet is dying .

The internet is just a delivery mechanism, and for people that see it for what it really is, the internet has never been more alive . I truly recommend using the internet as if it was 1999 .

Even on my phone, I’ve stopped using javascript frontends and embraced using eww in emacs (in termux), only falling back to fennec for about 5-10% of usecases:

I find this way of using the internet far higher in signal than any other method, allowing me to look up information, read documentation, and produce more.

For the uninitiated, emacs ships with EWW (Emacs Web Wowser) permitting you to browse the web with image and gif (when did gifs die, I almost never see them these days!) support directly inside Emacs.

I have some sane defaults that permit ease of use such as using B for back, U for yanking url at point, and a few built in functions.

Hitting R will invoke eww readable which is similar to reader mode in firefox, removing headers and footers and focusing in on the text on page. Useful.

You can send the page to your default browser with & . If a page doesn’t render nicely, this is a good fallback.

D will download images locally, b goes back a page, a will save bookmarks. All of this makes browsing in eww truly enjoyable.

I have also set .pdf to open in emacs, .mp4 and youtube/video hosting links to open in mpv, and gopher/gemini links to open in elpher. Elpher is the EWW for the gopher and gemini protocols, the smolweb that is all signal and no noise.

EWW uses Shr to render html, so you will see some callouts to that in my configuration below:

Here’s how I have configured EWW to work in my Emacs configuration :

(setq eww-search-prefix "https://searx.labrynth.org/search?q=")

(setq eww-download-directory (expand-file-name "~/Downloads/"))

(defun my-browse-url-mpv (url &rest _args)

(defun my-browse-url-pdf (url &rest _args)

"Fetch remote PDF and open in pdf-tools within Emacs."

(let ((tmp (make-temp-file "emacs-pdf-" nil ".pdf")))

'(("\\(youtube\\.com\\|youtu\\.be\\|vimeo\\.com\\|twitch\\.tv\\)" . my-browse-url-mpv)

("^gemini://" . elpher-browse-url-elpher)

("^gopher://" . elpher-browse-url-elpher)

(setq browse-url-secondary-browser-function 'browse-url-generic

(define-key eww-mode-map (kbd "=") #'text-scale-increase)

(define-key eww-mode-map (kbd "-") #'text-scale-decrease)

(define-key eww-mode-map (kbd "0") #'text-scale-adjust))

(defun my/eww-download-image-at-point ()

"Download image at point to `eww-download-directory'."

(let ((url (or (get-text-property (point) 'image-url)

(let* ((filename (file-name-nondirectory (url-filename (url-generic-parse-url url))))

items.title_ko: Emacs를 브라우저로 쓰기
items.summary_ko: 작성자는 Emacs를 유일한 작업 환경으로 삼기 위해 EWW로 웹을 탐색하고 있다. 며칠간 써 본 결과 일반적인 용도의 85~90%는 감당할 수 있었다고 평가한다. 또한 크롬이나 파이어폭스 같은 현대 브라우저는 산만해지기 쉬운 반면, 터미널 브라우저는 집중력을 지키는 데 도움이 된다고 말한다. 더불어 소셜 플랫폼의 제약에서 벗어나 자유로운 토론이 가능한 인터넷을 지향하는 입장을 밝힌다.
items.content_ko: 작성자는 Emacs를 유일한 컴퓨팅 환경으로 쓰려는 목표에 따라 Emacs 안에서 웹을 탐색하는 방식을 진지하게 고민하고 있다. 예전에는 EWW를 부가 기능 정도로만 생각했지만, 며칠 사용해 보니 자바스크립트가 많은 웹에서도 대부분의 용도에 쓸 만하다고 느꼈다. 작성자는 크롬이나 파이어폭스를 쓸 때 추천 콘텐츠와 여러 유혹 때문에 쉽게 산만해지고 하루를 잃게 된다고 말한다. 반면 EWW나 lynx, browsh 같은 터미널 브라우저를 쓰면 이런 문제가 크게 줄어든다고 한다. 또한 소셜 플랫폼의 제한된 프런트엔드와 폐쇄적인 공간에서 벗어나 더 자유로운 인터넷으로 나아가야 한다는 생각을 밝힌다. 작성자는 빅테크 플랫폼에 너무 많은 것을 내주었고 얻은 것은 적다고 주장한다.

items.title: Let Me Let You Own Your Data
items.content:
Why do I have to choose between my web app respecting people’s privacy and it, like… having basic functionality?

When I was working on Cheapskate , I realized after a few weeks that there was a fundamental issue. The app relies on Supabase for the unsexy parts of its architecture: authentication and a SQL datastore. All of it is bog-standard and all of it I happily handed off to be someone else’s problem. To be clear, I love Supabase – if I had to run all that boilerplate myself, I never would have made Cheapskate.

But… the shape of it is wrong. I don’t want to own this data. This is a person’s financial details! Shouldn’t that live with them, and not with me? Is it even possible to make a web app like this, with anything close to the same convenience and functionality (durable, works across devices, shareable with friends) as Supabase allows?

items.title: Instagram Meta AI Vulnerability: How Hackers Bypassed 2FA with Prompt Injection
items.content:
Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 1: A new exploit, which is even worse than this one is currently doing rounds on telegram. Details unknown at this time. Unpatched at the time of writing.

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

A logical flaw in Meta’s AI-powered Instagram account recovery assistant let attackers bypass two-factor authentication entirely not by cracking a code or intercepting an SMS, but by talking the chatbot into doing the work for them. High-value “OG” Instagram handles worth hundreds of thousands of dollars were stolen and resold on Telegram within minutes of each compromise. The dormant Obama White House account got hijacked. Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

items.title: Meta and TikTok Have Been Secretly Paying Millions of Dollars to Teens to Keep Their Experiences Out of Court: The companies "offered so much money that my clients could not refuse."
items.content:
It’s more apparent than ever just how harmful social media is to the impressionable minds of teens.

But that’s not a story that social platforms want you to hear. According to explosive new reporting by Bloomberg , both Meta and TikTok secretly paid off a dozen teen plaintiffs in settlements most of which ranged anywhere from $2 million to $2.5 million in a bid to keep their claims out of the public eye.

The teen plaintiffs accused the companies of causing their depression, self-harm, eating disorders, and anxiety. According to the publication’s insider sources, Meta paid just two teens a combined $7 million to keep them quiet — a startling revelation that highlights how far these companies are willing to keep a highly sensitive subject out of the headlines.

Experts say it’s also a part of a broader effort to discourage other plaintiffs to come forward, a gambit that isn’t exactly paying off. Per Bloomberg , there are almost 10,000 personal injury cases still pending in both state and federal courts against Meta, YouTube, Snapchat, and TikTok following landmark trials that opened the floodgates. Over 1,000 school districts are also accusing social media companies of harming students, prioritizing profits over the safety of underage users.

In other words, despite its efforts to keep teen plaintiffs quiet by paying them millions of dollars, the companies are still exposed to plenty of liability, which could add up to almost $400 billion, according to Bloomberg ’s estimates.

The social media companies “offered so much money that my clients could not refuse,” trial attorney Mark Lanier, who represents two of the teen plaintiffs, told Bloomberg . “These are not insignificant numbers.”

“I believe they are the first dominoes to fall in what will be a succession of dominoes to come,” he added.

items.content_ko: 소셜미디어가 청소년의 정신 건강에 얼마나 해로운지는 점점 더 분명해지고 있다. 그러나 Bloomberg의 새 보도에 따르면 Meta와 TikTok은 10대 원고 십여 명과 합의하면서 그 내용이 공개되지 않도록 비밀리에 합의금을 지급했다. 합의금 대부분은 200만 달러에서 250만 달러 사이로 알려졌다. 원고들은 두 회사 때문에 우울증, 자해, 섭식장애, 불안이 생겼다고 주장했다. 내부 소식통에 따르면 Meta는 그중 두 명에게 합계 700만 달러를 지급했다. 전문가들은 이것이 다른 원고들이 나서지 못하도록 막으려는 더 큰 전략의 일부라고 본다. 다만 이 전략이 항상 성공하는 것은 아니다. Bloomberg에 따르면 주요 재판 이후 Meta, YouTube, Snapchat, TikTok을 상대로 한 개인 상해 소송이 주州 법원과 연방 법원에 약 1만 건 남아 있다. 1,000여 개 학군도 소셜미디어 기업이 학생들에게 해를 끼쳤다며 소송을 제기했다.

items.title: KDE Plasma 6.9 Will Launch XWayland Only When Needed
items.content:
KDE developers are preparing an important change for the upcoming Plasma 6.9 desktop environment, scheduled for release in late February. According to the latest update, XWayland, the compatibility layer that allows X11 applications to run in Wayland sessions, will now start only when needed instead of running continuously in the background.

Until now, Plasma kept XWayland active even when no X11 applications ran. The change means that Plasma’s Wayland session will no longer need to keep XWayland running simply to support applications that users may never launch.

Apart from this improvement, Plasma 6.9 is receiving a redesigned Task Switching page in System Settings. The page was ported to QML, with a refreshed interface that also includes configuration options for the Overview effect.

The Date & Time settings page is also undergoing a similar transition. Its new QML-based interface consolidates controls into a single page, making it quicker to change the system’s time zone.

KDE is also refining desktop customization. The wallpaper configuration page will have more room for browsing images after the desktop layout selector moved to a separate page. Moreover, desktop icons and the Folder View widget will gain additional size options, filling a noticeable gap between the two largest existing sizes.

Regarding performance improvements, Spectacle, KDE’s screenshot utility, will launch faster thanks to optimizations and parallelization. The Add Widgets sidebar has also been optimized to open substantially faster, with smoother animations.

On top of that, the Task Manager will handle window previews more efficiently by avoiding unnecessary thumbnail regeneration when the pointer leaves and returns to a preview, thus eliminating a minor flickering issue. Additionally, when a grouped application requests attention, opening its group popup will now identify the specific window responsible.

On the network management side, users will be able to forget saved connections directly from the Networks widget without opening System Settings. The network share configuration wizard will also automatically recognize more information from pasted URLs, including the protocol and whether encryption is required.

For system monitoring, Plasma 6.9 adds a sensor showing the number of physical CPU cores, available in both the System Monitor application and its widgets.

Other desktop refinements include named presets for the Wobbly Windows effect, fade animations for Spectacle’s screen capture overlay, and more convenient duration editing in the Timer widget. The Keyboard settings page will make it clearer when the system-wide keyboard layout is used rather than a custom configuration.

Finally, if the login via Plasma Login Manager fails, it will provide a basic terminal fallback instead of leaving users with a black screen, allowing them to access the system for troubleshooting.

For more information about the upcoming changes, see KDE’s “ This Week in Plasma ” blog post.
items.title_ko: KDE Plasma 6.9, XWayland를 필요할 때만 실행
items.summary_ko: KDE Plasma 6.9는 2월 말 출시 예정이며, XWayland가 항상 백그라운드에서 돌아가지 않고 X11 애플리케이션이 필요할 때만 시작된다. 시스템 설정의 작업 전환 페이지는 QML로 옮겨져 새로 디자인되었고, Overview 효과 설정 옵션이 추가되었다. 날짜 및 시간 설정 페이지도 QML 기반으로 바뀌어 시간대를 더 빨리 변경할 수 있게 되었다.
items.content_ko: KDE 개발자들은 다가오는 Plasma 6.9 데스크톱 환경에 중요한 변경을 준비 중이며, 출시는 2월 말로 예정되어 있다. 최신 업데이트에 따르면 Wayland 세션에서 X11 애플리케이션을 실행하게 해 주는 호환 계층 XWayland는 이제 백그라운드에서 계속 실행되지 않고 필요할 때만 시작된다. 지금까지 Plasma는 X11 앱을 전혀 쓰지 않아도 XWayland를 계속 켜 두었다. 이 변경으로 Plasma의 Wayland 세션은 사용자가 실행할지도 모르는 앱을 위해 XWayland를 상시 구동할 필요가 없어진다. 이 밖에도 Plasma 6.9에서는 시스템 설정의 작업 전환 페이지가 새로 디자인되어 QML로 옮겨지고, Overview 효과의 설정 옵션이 포함된다. 날짜 및 시간 설정 페이지도 비슷하게 바뀐다. 새 QML 기반 인터페이스는 설정을 한 페이지에 모아 시스템 시간대를 더 빠르게 바꿀 수 있게 한다. 데스크톱 꾸미기 기능도 다듬어진다. 데스크톱 레이아웃 선택기가 별도 페이지로 옮겨지면서 배경화면 설정 페이지에 이미지를 둘러볼 공간이 더 생긴다.

items.title: 디시 해킹들
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Periodic-Oriented Programming for FIRST Robotics
items.content:
I recently retired from mentoring my FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) team. I started as a student in 2010, and went straight into mentoring upon graduation, so in total I have been writing FRC programs for about 17 years.

Over time though I've become more and more dismayed with how FRC programs are typically written. For decades, I feel that FIRST and WPILib have encouraged students to severely overengineer their robot programs. As time has gone on, I have become more and more frustrated with the state of FRC programming, and our team's code style has drifted further and further away from the norm.

To be clear, I have the utmost respect for the time and effort that FIRST and the WPILib maintainers put in every year, and it is thanks to their efforts that FRC teams have reliable and complete libraries every year. But I think the accepted programming practices in FRC are leading students astray and ought to be corrected.

So as I step away from FIRST , I decided I should write down my philosophy of robot programming in FRC, which I have decided to give the pithy name of Periodic-Oriented Programming .

Periodic-Oriented Programming is very simple: Do as much as possible in your periodic function. Uses very few abstractions, and write most of your logic in one big function, top to bottom. This is so simple and beginner-like that it seems like it shouldn't work for serious programs. But it does, as long as you carefully establish a few simple boundaries and practices.

For context, the essential structure of an FRC program is typically to use the TimedRobot framework provided by WPILib. To use it, you simply implement periodic functions and the robot framework calls them 50 times per second. For example, here's a complete "tank drive" robot program in Python:

self . gamepad = wpilib . XboxController ( 0 )

self . leftMotor = rev . SparkMax ( 10 , rev . SparkLowLevel . MotorType . kBrushless )

self . rightMotor = rev . SparkMax ( 11 , rev . SparkLowLevel . MotorType . kBrushless )

self . leftMotor . set ( self . gamepad . getLeftY ())

self . rightMotor . set ( self . gamepad . getRightY ())

50 times per second, the left and right motor speeds will be updated to use the left and right gamepad axes. The robot framework and hardware abstraction layers do the rest.

In essence, every FRC program does the following work in periodic :

Compute the desired state of the hardware (motor speeds, actuator positions, etc.)

Enforce safety constraints, smooth signals, or otherwise process the outputs

In Periodic-Oriented Programming, I basically encourage my students to lean into this pattern. POP code should have few abstractions, and most of the logic should be written top-to-bottom in a single function. And to the greatest extent possible, everything should be run on every periodic —no modes, no commands, no state.

As programs get larger, more structure is needed, but the core philosophy remains the same. The most important piece of structure is subsystems .

The use of "subsystem" classes will be familiar to most FRC teams, but the specifics are what matter here:

Every subsystem has a periodic method. This is called from robotPeriodic so it runs 100% of the time.

Hardware is never accessible outside the subsystem. All access to the hardware must be mediated through subsystem methods.

These rules extend the Periodic-Orientation into the subsystem code. For each subsystem, all of its logic should be centralized in one function and readable top to bottom. In most cases, the subsystem periodic is the only place in the entire program that actually touches the hardware. This has many advantages: it ensures by construction that hardware is only touched once per tick, that safety constraints are respected 100% of the time, and that logging and telemetry are run consistently.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title_ko: 제로데이 취약점, Windows 11 BitLocker 기본 보호 완전히 우회
items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: Eric Trump-backed robot soldier startup can’t pay staff after founder borrowed $4.6 million from company to buy home
items.content:
Foundation Future Industries , a maker of military humanoid robots advised and backed by Eric Trump, failed to pay employees last month as its cash reserves dwindled, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter.

Workers have yet to receive paychecks after San Francisco-based Foundation missed payroll on Oct. 30, said the people, who asked for anonymity to speak candidly about a private company.

The situation has particularly angered some inside the startup because its CEO and co-founder, Sankaet Pathak , borrowed $4.6 million from the company last year to buy a luxury home, money that could have been used to pay workers, the people said.

Public records show that an LLC that names Pathak as sole principal purchased a $4.6 million Sausalito, California, property with "sweeping, cinematic views" of the San Francisco Bay in October 2025.

A spokesman for Pathak acknowledged receiving a detailed list of the major points from this story on Thursday, but didn't respond to requests for comment. Pathak's previous startup, a fintech firm named Synapse, collapsed in 2024, leaving thousands of Americans locked out of their savings accounts .

Foundation's cash crunch comes at a precarious moment for the company, which Pathak has said is close to unveiling a next-generation, weapons-ready robot that will help the U.S. compete against Chinese rivals. At the same time, Pathak is seeking to raise hundreds of millions of dollars in funding at a $3 billion valuation.

The company has garnered headlines this year for Pathak's claims that his robots could soon take on battlefield tasks in Ukraine or patrol the U.S. border with Mexico. Broadcast interviews and articles about Foundation also include claims that the company has won $24 million in Pentagon contracts.

"What we're about to unveil in the next couple of months [is] going to be the strongest humanoid robot that exists anywhere in the world, including China," Pathak said in an April television interview.

That April interview introduced Eric Trump, the son of the U.S. president, as a Foundation investor and chief strategy advisor. It is unclear how large his stake is.

Eric Trump and his brother Donald Trump Jr. have invested in an array of defense firms, including makers of military drones and autonomous weapons. A July Washington Post investigation found that startups backed by investment vehicles linked to the brothers had secured at least $3.2 billion in government business.

"We have to win robotics in the United States of America," Eric Trump said in April. "When you go up and interact with these robots ... they fist bump you, they high five you, they follow your commands."

Eric Trump's involvement in Foundation drew the swift ire of Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., who asked whether Foundation won U.S. defense contracts because of nepotism.

"Eric Trump went on FOX to brag about winning ANOTHER multimillion-dollar contract from the Trump administration," Warren said in an April 23 social media post. "This looks like corruption in plain sight."

Eric Trump didn't respond to requests for comment. His spokesperson recently told the Financial Times that Eric Trump had "no involvement in Foundation's management, operations, strategic decisions or commercial activities, including the solicitation, negotiation, procurement or execution of any government contracts."

While the Eric Trump announcement created speculation within Foundation that a Democratic-led Congress may look to investigate the company, Foundation itself didn't actually win the $24 million in contracts, despite that assertion being widely reported across news outlets.

Instead, it acquired Florida-based Boardwalk Robotics in late 2024, and government research contracts won by that firm account for the claim, said a person with knowledge of the matter. Foundation used Boardwalk's robot Alex as the basis for its first robot, the Phantom MK-1, this person said.

Pathak의 대변인은 기사 요지를 받았다고 확인했지만 취재 요청에는 응답하지 않았다. 이전 스타트업인 핀테크 기업 Synapse는 2024년 붕괴해 수많은 미국인이 저축 계좌에 접근하지 못하게 된 바 있다.

items.title: Nextcloud Releases Free Desktop Office Suite Built on Euro-Office
items.content:
Nextcloud has announced its new Office Desktop app, a free, open-source office suite powered by Euro-Office , for Linux, Windows, and macOS. The application allows users to create and edit documents locally, work offline, and collaborate with others through Nextcloud Hub.

The desktop application was announced in September as part of Nextcloud Hub 26 Summer. Now, ready-to-use builds are available for download, letting users install the office suite directly on their computers without a Nextcloud server for local document editing.

Nextcloud releases a free desktop office suite built on Euro-Office.

For those unfamiliar, Euro-Office is a European-led open-source project based on a fork of the ONLYOFFICE codebase, licensed under AGPLv3. It was established to improve development transparency, simplify external contributions, and provide an independently governed office solution.

According to its maintainers, the decision to fork ONLYOFFICE followed concerns about limited upstream collaboration, difficulties building the software from source, and proprietary components in parts of its ecosystem. The project is supported by several European technology companies and organizations, including Nextcloud, IONOS, OpenProject, Proton, and XWiki.

As for the new desktop application, it includes editors for text documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and PDFs. It supports Microsoft’s DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX formats alongside OpenDocument formats such as ODT, ODS, and ODP.

One of its selling points is offline operations. Users can open, edit, and save documents directly on their computers without an internet connection. When connected to a Nextcloud instance, the application provides access to cloud-stored files and enables real-time collaborative editing.

Moreover, users can connect multiple Nextcloud instances to the same application, allowing them to work with documents stored across different servers without switching between separate desktop clients.

The application also uses fonts installed locally on the operating system, including custom and corporate fonts. Other capabilities include digital document signatures, password protection, and restrictions on editing, commenting, and form filling.

Regarding platform availability, Linux users can download DEB packages for Debian and Ubuntu or RPM packages for Fedora and other RPM-based distributions. Windows builds are available for x64 and ARM64 systems, while macOS support currently targets Apple Silicon.

Nextcloud distributes signed builds intended for production use, while the Euro-Office project also provides unsigned community builds for testing and development. Both versions are built from the same source code, which is publicly available on GitHub .

The Nextcloud Office Desktop app is available now from the official announcement , which also includes installation details and instructions for connecting the application to Nextcloud Hub.
items.title_ko: Nextcloud, Euro-Office 기반 무료 데스크톱 오피스 스위트 출시
items.summary_ko: Nextcloud가 Linux, Windows, macOS용 무료 오픈소스 오피스 스위트 Office Desktop 앱을 공개했다. 이 앱은 Euro-Office를 기반으로 하며, 문서를 로컬에서 만들고 편집하고 오프라인으로 작업할 수 있으며 Nextcloud Hub를 통해 다른 사람과 협업할 수 있다. Euro-Office는 ONLYOFFICE 코드베이스를 포크한 유럽 주도 오픈소스 프로젝트로 AGPLv3 라이선스를 따른다.
items.content_ko: Nextcloud는 Linux, Windows, macOS를 지원하는 새 Office Desktop 앱을 발표했다. 이는 Euro-Office 기반의 무료 오픈소스 오피스 스위트다. 사용자는 이 앱으로 문서를 로컬에서 만들고 편집할 수 있으며, 오프라인으로도 작업할 수 있고, Nextcloud Hub를 통해 다른 사람과 협업할 수 있다. 이 데스크톱 앱은 9월 Nextcloud Hub 26 Summer의 일부로 처음 소개되었고, 이제 바로 사용할 수 있는 빌드를 내려받을 수 있다. Nextcloud 서버 없이도 설치해 로컬 문서 편집에 쓸 수 있다. Euro-Office는 ONLYOFFICE 코드베이스를 포크한 유럽 주도 오픈소스 프로젝트로, AGPLv3 라이선스를 따른다. 프로젝트 측은 ONLYOFFICE의 상류 협업이 제한적이고 소스 빌드가 어렵고 생태계 일부에 독점 구성요소가 있다는 우려 때문에 포크를 결정했다고 설명한다. 이 프로젝트는 여러 유럽 기술 기업과 단체의 지원을 받고 있다.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-123638 📢 Source: Gitea 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False The "Protected file patterns" setting of a branch protection rule was checked against file names as git prints them, and git quotes names that contain a double quote, a backslash or a control character. Such names never matched a pattern, so a user with write access could add or change files under a protected pattern by direct push or through a pull request merge, and could move a protected file out of the pattern's reach by renaming it. Where the patterns protect workflow files, this allowed adding a workflow that then ran on the repository's runners. Changed files are now listed unquoted, and a rename reports both the old and the new path. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-15T21:14:03.522Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-123638
